questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, how can you help others see you?

options.text: Ride with your headlight off.
Wear bright clothing.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Do not use turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to be more visible. Always use your headlight and use your turn signals.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if the clothing is very loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good clothing reduces injury in a crash. Choose a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. They should be made of sturdy material and fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: For best protection, motorcycle pants should be made of:

options.text: Soft material.
Heavy material.
Material loose enough to flap in the wind.
Short material that exposes some leg.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. The pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use that lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you inspect before riding?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires.
How much cushion your seat has.
The shine of your paint.
The wind direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Why is space between your motorcycle and other vehicles important?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
It lets you depend on others to see hazards.
It requires you to go faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and bright-colored clothing when riding. Crashes happen during the day and at night, so be visible at all times.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that lets you draft off other vehicles.
The one where other drivers can see you.
The one in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one where other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where you can see others and they can see you. Avoid other drivers' blind spots, wind blasts, and surface hazards. Your position should discourage sharing your lane and give you an escape route. Maximize your space cushion.

questions.question: What makes a helmet provide the best protection?

options.text: It meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
It looks sturdy.
It is inexpensive.
It is your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: It meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should motorcycle riders watch for?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking space.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
Oncoming traffic.
Noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. Drivers may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?

options.text: A landing strip
An oily or greasy strip
Lane markings
Ice

questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars collect in the center of each lane. It is usually safe for a motorcycle to ride on this strip if the road is dry.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of crashing, you should:

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Look only at your mirrors.
Rely on your side vision.
Slow down so vehicles in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: Unlike food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
Alcohol is never removed from the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes because it does not need to be digested. Your body removes alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Ride like you would on your bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: Crashes happen most often among:

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Those familiar with their motorcycle.
Those who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often for new, untrained riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part closest to the shoulder.
Where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in a position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit until the pass is done.
You can ignore "No passing zone" markings if you start in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must pass within the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must pass within the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Means your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. The time needed varies by person, so it is safest not to ride after any alcohol.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to the frame.
Ride with your headlight on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright, reflective clothing and use your turn signals and brake light.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when stopping will take longer. This gives you more time and space to stop safely.

questions.question: If you must ride over an object or uneven surface you cannot avoid, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat to let your legs absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat to let your legs absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb the impact. Just before hitting the obstacle, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What is an advantage of wearing a leather jacket when riding?

options.text: It makes a rider look cool.
It is usually too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
It should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally leather, when riding. Leather protects you in a crash. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: How can someone be excused from taking the motorcycle skills test?

options.text: By completing an approved rider training course
By scoring 95 percent or higher on the written test
By having no moving violations on their record
By applying in certain counties

questions.correctAnswerText: By completing an approved rider training course
questions.explanation: You can be excused from the skills test if you complete an approved rider training course that includes a similar skills test.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same way as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be operated in curves.
It should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or a motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: How can you make night riding safer?

options.text: Avoid riding at night.
Wear reflective clothing.
Other drivers cannot see your turn signals at night.
Only ride at night in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when riding?

options.text: Look ahead and watch for potential hazards.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Do not worry about hazards because they are minimal.
Look ahead but do not search for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and watch for potential hazards.
questions.explanation: Always look well ahead of your vehicle. This helps you see hazards before you reach them and gives you time to react.

questions.question: What type of helmet provides the best protection?

options.text: One that fits snugly.
One that is well-worn and broken in.
One that is loose.
One without a chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.
